why: Story 45.7, FR-180, AD-65. The pinning between keeper_core::file_asset::parse_file_url and the TypeScript composer src/lib/viewers/file-asset-url.ts. Rust parses the URL a <video src> carries; TypeScript writes it. They never meet at runtime, so the only thing that can stop them drifting is a table both test suites load from THIS file. 'ok' round-trips: the composer must produce url from the two halves, and the parser must take url back apart into the same two halves. 'refused' is the belt-and-braces pair: the composer still produces a URL for a dot segment, deliberately, so a traversal attempt reaches the log as visible text rather than as a path that already collapsed - and the parser refuses every one of them. Encoding is RFC 3986's unreserved set (alphanumeric plus - . _ ~), which is keeper/src/notes_vault.rs::asset_url's set exactly, so keeper has ONE spelling for an asset URL rather than one per scheme. That is stricter than encodeURIComponent, which leaves ! ' ( ) * unescaped; those are legal sub-delims in a path segment, and escaping them anyway costs nothing and removes a question about what a webview will normalise.
